parole.testo: From Latin amalgama, from Medieval Latin amalgama (“mercury alloy”), from Arabic اَلْمَلْغَم (al-malḡam, “emollient poultice or unguent for sores”), from Ancient Greek μάλαγμα (málagma, “emollient; malleable material”), from μαλάσσω (malássō, “to soften”), from μαλακός (malakós, “soft”).
Likely borrowed from Latin mumia, ultimately from Arabic مُومِيَاء (mūmiyāʔ), from Classical Persian مُومِیَا (mūmiyā).

parole.significato: figure, digit, cipher, numeral (a symbol representing a number)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Latin cifra, ultimately from Arabic صِفْر (ṣifr, “zero”). Doublet of шифр (šifr).
